sources.entry: Econumo - Budgeting application for managing personal and family finances, supporting multiple currencies, joint accounts, and budgets. (Demo, Source Code) MIT Docker

summary.one_liner: Econumo is a self-hosted personal finance and budgeting app, shipped as a single Go binary in a Docker image with a React web UI.
summary.what_it_does: The app runs as one self-contained Go binary that serves both the API and the web app, and applies database migrations automatically on boot. It defaults to SQLite and can be switched to PostgreSQL through the DATABASE_URL setting. Configuration lives in a .env file, with .env.example documenting the database, mail, currencies, CORS and logging options. Password-recovery email is enabled by setting MAILER_DSN. CLI commands such as creating users or updating currency rates run through the binary inside the container. The README also describes a health endpoint at /health and a locales/ folder of JSON translation catalogues for contributing new languages. Upgrading from the v0.x PHP version is described as a migration that reuses the existing database.
use_cases: Manage personal finances on a home server
Migrate from Econumo v0.x PHP to v1.x
Send password-recovery email for a self-hosted finance app
Run a finance app without Docker under systemd
how_to_run: docker compose pull && docker compose up -d
Open the web UI in a browser and create the first user
docker compose exec econumo /app/econumo user:create "Name" user@example.com password (optional CLI user creation)
notable: Single self-contained Go binary with the web UI embedded; the README says it uses up to about 10 MB of RAM
Works with SQLite by default and PostgreSQL via DATABASE_URL
Database migrations run automatically on startup
Translations kept in the repository as JSON files, with key and placeholder parity checked by the test suite
Optional MCP setup for connecting Claude or Codex to an instance
caveats: Upgrading from v0.x (PHP) requires following the separate migration guide, and the old Docker Hub image is no longer updated
The README does not describe the feature set beyond the setup, so budgeting features such as multi-currency and joint accounts are only taken from the listing metadata
Some setup details, such as the full configuration reference and the non-Docker walkthrough, are in external docs not included in the README
